entry.title: The Most Annoying Form Ever...
entry.summary:
This is a submission for the DEV April Fools Challenge I built the Annoying Form App — a beautifully designed, psychologically exhausting web form that turns a simple task into a battle of patience. This project explores a bold anti-UX philosophy: what if forms actively fought back? Instead of helping users submit data, this app: Shrinks inputs while you're typing It’s a premium-looking interface with the soul of pure chaos. https://github.com/riyaz489/chaotic_form/blob/main/src/assets/demo.gif https://github.com/riyaz489/chaotic_form This project was built entirely using Antigravity, without writing a single line of code manually. Instead of traditional development, I approached this like a “prompt-driven chaos experiment”: I described the app’s behavior in natural language focusing on how a form could become increasingly frustrating Key Ideas Behind the Build The biggest challenge wasn’t building features — it was making them frustrating in a consistent and believable way. 🤖 Best Google AI Usage This entire project was built using Antigravity, without writing a single line of code manually. Instead of traditional development, I described increasingly chaotic and frustrating UX behaviours From shrinking inputs to teleporting text and infinite popups, every piece of chaos was orchestrated through AI. Ironically, a tool designed to boost developer productivity was used here to create something that destroys user productivity. This project is essentially: “What happens when you give AI full control… and terrible intentions.” ☕ Best Ode to Larry Masinter Inspired by the legendary absurdity of HTTP 418 I'm a teapot, this project embraces the same philosophy: It looks like a serious, premium product Just like a teapot refusing to brew coffee, It’s a tribute to the playful, bizarre side of the web, where: Uselessness is intentional, and frustration is the feature.
